title: NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) — Cancellation Refund Calculation
content:
Refund calculation for a cancelled policy under the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own).

## A. Request, reason and date

The signed request a cancellation refund means is the one the risk premium cancellation credit booked at processing references or, when the risk premium credit was zero and none was booked, the latest signed cancellation request received on the policy, a withdrawn or unsigned request not counting, and its reason is the cancellation reason the cancelled policy shows. The cancellation effective date is the one the cancelled policy shows. A reason refunds from inception when it is a duplicate NFIP policy or a loan closing that did not occur.

## B. What the refund adds up

For a cancellation refund, and only for it, the risk premium credit is booked when the cancellation is processed and the ICC premium, Reserve Fund Assessment, HFIAA surcharge, Federal Policy Fee and probation surcharge credits when the refund is disbursed, each referencing the cancellation request, and the refund paid to the payor of record is all those credits plus, for a cancellation refund whose current term and the term before it together carry at most one premium-bearing endorsement and at most one re-rate credit, each counted by its risk premium entries, the premium received but not owed, while a cancellation refund whose terms carry more than one premium-bearing endorsement or more than one re-rate credit is the total of its credits alone, as the base refund method restated in section C sets out; every other refund remains the total of the credits it settles. The cancellation refund adds up every cancellation credit referencing the signed request, those booked at processing and those this refund books, and, where the booking sentence above adds it, the premium received but not owed; each credit is rounded half-up to the cent before they are added, and the refund is never below zero.

## C. Scope

For the ICC premium, Reserve Fund Assessment, HFIAA surcharge, Federal Policy Fee and probation surcharge credits a cancellation refund books, and only for those credits, and only while the current term and the term before it together carry at most one premium-bearing endorsement and at most one re-rate credit, each counted by its risk premium entries, the reason's refund method is applied over the current term and the term before it as this calculation sets out, and amounts of terms earlier than that are returned only through the NFIP Bureau. When those terms carry more than one premium-bearing endorsement or more than one re-rate credit, the case the premium-received and fee sentences of this rule leave to the base clause, the base clause applies to those credits as written: full from inception returns every component booked on the policy, fees included; current term full returns the current term's ICC premium, Reserve Fund Assessment and HFIAA surcharge in full; pro rata returns those of the current term multiplied by the days from the cancellation effective date to the term end divided by the days from the term start to the term end; under current term full and pro rata the Federal Policy Fee and probation surcharge are fully earned, the claim bar of section E applies, and the refund is the total of the credits. The risk premium credit follows the cancellation processing rule.

## D. The credits

The ICC premium and the Reserve Fund Assessment of the current term are returned for the days from the cancellation effective date to the term end over the days of the current term, the Federal Policy Fee and probation surcharge are fully earned, and no premium is treated as received but not owed. The HFIAA surcharge is returned the way the risk premium is: when the cancellation took effect before the current term start, the current term's HFIAA surcharge in full and the term before it for the days from the cancellation effective date to the current term start over the days of the current term, or in full when the cancellation took effect on or before that term's start; otherwise the current term's HFIAA surcharge for the days from the cancellation effective date to the term end over the days of the current term. For the refund credits the term before the current one ends at the current term start and its days are counted as those of the current term.

## E. Claim bar

For the ICC premium, Reserve Fund Assessment and HFIAA surcharge credits a cancellation refund books for the current term, and only for those credits, the claim bar is read as follows; the risk premium credit follows the cancellation processing rule's claim bar. Under a reason that bars a refund once a claim has been paid — mortgage paid off, voluntary — not required, replaced by private flood, and removed from the Special Flood Hazard Area by a Letter of Map Amendment or Revision — when the cancellation took effect in the current term and a loss dated on or after the current term start carries claim payments, net of the payment items voided, above zero, nothing of the current term is returned. When the records cannot place such a paid loss on either side of the current term start, that is when no loss dated after the month band around the current term start carries such payments, a loss dated in that band does, and the latest loss on which a claim payment was ever issued is dated after the band, or is dated in the band on or after the current term start with its payments all voided, the month band being the losses dated as many whole calendar months before the processing date as the current term start is, the current term's return is held: nothing of the current term is returned by these credits and the other parts are returned as worked out. In every other case no refund at all is due for the current term under those reasons when a claim with a date of loss in the current term has been paid or is still open.

## F. Worked figure (hypothetical)

Building sold; cancellation effective with 100 days left of a 365-day current term; risk premium credit booked at processing 1,000.00; current term ICC premium 73.00, Reserve Fund Assessment 365.00, HFIAA surcharge 182.50; no claims. ICC 20.00; Reserve Fund Assessment 100.00; HFIAA 50.00; fees fully earned; nothing received but not owed. Refund: 1,000.00 plus 20.00 plus 100.00 plus 50.00, which is 1,170.00.
